newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Mexico's Zedillo flies to Argentina for trade talks.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo flies to Argentina for trade talks.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo on Tuesday starts a three-day visit to Argentina aimed at boosting bilateral political ties and pushing forward free trade talks with Mercosur, South America's main trade bloc.

"We are re-starting the Mexico-Mercosur negotiations," Mexico's Trade Undersecretary Jaime Zabludovsky told Reuters. Mercosur is a customs union including South American giants Brazil and Argentina, plus neighbouring Uruguay and Paraguay.
Zedillo and his Argentine counterpart Carlos Menem plan to sign an agreement for the mutual protection of investments.
"Then, in a second stage, we will seek a more broad and ambitious deal so that businessmen from both countries can make more and better deals," Zabludovsky said.

He said Mexico -- a member of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) with the United States and Canada -- and Mercosur nations have already exchanged blueprints for a trade deal. "In the coming months we will do the same with tariffs lists in order to keep moving forward."

In an interview published on Sunday by a Buenos Aires daily, Zedillo said he would seek both a political and economic alliance with Argentina in order to give the two countries a bigger say in international affairs.

"We are intermediate countries in the concert of nations and we may be weak in front of the powerful," he said. "But if we can harmonise our views in multilateral forums and in our bilateral ties, I think it will be in our mutual benefit."
He also said an agreement with Argentina should take precedence over a deal with Mercosur. Trade between the two countries this year was $520 million, with a $140 million surplus for Mexico.
Zedillo, who will arrive from Chile where both he and Menem attended a regional summit, will be accompanied by 40 businessmen on his trip to Argentina.

On Tuesday he plans to deliver a speech at the Argentine Council for International Relations and visit the Buenos Aires stock exchange, and on Wednesday he will have more talks with Menem and visit Congress.
